'''Shlomo Margel''' ({{langx|he|שלמה מרגל}}; born 9 October 1945) is a Professor of [[Chemistry]] at [[Bar Ilan University]] specializing in [[polymer]]s, [[biopolymer]]s, functional [[thin film]]s, [[Molecular encapsulation|encapsulation]], [[Surface science#Surface chemistry|surface chemistry]], [[nanotechnology]], [[nanobiotechnology]] and agro-nanotechnology.<ref>[http://www.agri.gov.il/download/volcanipedia/Content/Eng/Vv4/#PDF/4-5 Message from the Editors, "Agro-nanotechnology in the Volcani Center", Volcani Voice, Vol.4, September 2017]</ref>

==Early life==
Shlomo Margel<ref>[https://research.biu.ac.il/labs/prof-margels-lab/ Prof. Margel, Bar-Ilan University Research Authority]</ref> was born in 1945 in [[Israel]] during the [[Mandatory Palestine|Mandate era]] into a seven-generation [[Jerusalem]]ite family. The Margel family descended from the [[:he:קטגוריה:משפחת לעוי-וייספיש-בהר"ן|Loewy]] ({{langx|he|לעווי}}),<ref>''Our forefathers at the gates of Jerusalem - from the disciples of the Vilna Ga'on following his Torah'', the genealogy of the Levine family, Jerusalem, 2011. In Hebrew: ''אבותינו בשערי ירושלים'' - מתלמידי הגר"א בעקבות תורתו, ירושלים, ה'תשע"ח</ref><ref>ספר היחס למשפחת לווין - כתב ר' יצחק דויד אשר לעווין, דפוס האחים רוחלר, ירושלים, ה'תרפ"ט</ref> [[:he:מנחם מנדל משקלוב|Menachem Mendel]] ({{langx|he|מנחם מנדל משקלוב}}) and [[Rivlin]] families. Their family trees merged several generations ago<ref>{{cite book| author = Morgenstern, Arie | year = 2007| title = The Return to Jerusalem: The Jewish Resettlement of Israel, 1800-1860| publisher = [[Shalem Center]] Press| isbn = 978-965-7052-40-2|url=http://www.kotar.co.il/KotarApp/Viewer.aspx?nBookID=94343413#1.0.6.default}}</ref><ref>אלעזר הורביץ, '''מוסד היסוד''' תולדות ראשית היישוב בירושלים על ידי תלמידי הגר"א</ref> and they were all students of the [[Vilna Gaon|Vilna Gaon (HaGra)]].<ref>a.k.a. ''[[Perushim]]'' (Hebrew: [[:he:עליית תלמידי הגר"א|עליית תלמידי הגר"א]]), disciples of the Vilna Gaon who left Lithuania at the beginning of the 19th century to settle in the Land of Israel.</ref>

==Academic career==
He obtained his Ph.D. from the Department of [[Materials Science]] at the [[Weizmann Institute of Science]] in 1976, followed by three years as a postdoctoral fellow at the Department of [[Inorganic Chemistry]], [[California Institute of Technology]] (Caltech). In 1988 he joined the [[Bar-Ilan University|Bar-Ilan Department of Chemistry]]<ref>[http://ch.biu.ac.il/margel Prof. Margel's Lab - Chemistry Department, Bar-Ilan University]</ref> and has risen through the ranks to full professor in 1994. Margel was a visiting scientist in [[DuPont Central Research]], Wilmington, Delaware, in the [[University of Ulm]], Germany, in [[Tokyo Institute of Technology]], Japan and in [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] (MIT), Institute for Soldiers' Nanotechnologies.<ref>[http://isnweb.mit.edu/ The Institute for Soldier Nanotechnologies]</ref> Margel chaired the Bar-Ilan Chemistry Department (1999-2001),<ref>[http://ch.biu.ac.il/ Department of Chemistry, Bar-Ilan University]</ref> served as the dean of the Bar-Ilan Faculty of Exact Sciences (2002-2003)<ref>[https://www1.biu.ac.il/en-why_exact_sciences Bar-Ilan Faculty of Exact Sciences]</ref> and was the Bar-Ilan [[Dean (education)|dean of students]] (2011-2014).<ref>[https://www.biu.ac.il/Dean/index.shtml Bar-Ilan, Dean of Students website]</ref> He was the head of the National Committee for [[Chemistry education|Chemistry in High School Education]] (2000-2003)<ref>[http://cms.education.gov.il/EducationCMS/UNITS/Mazkirut_Pedagogit/Chimya The Israeli National Committee for Chemistry in High School Education]</ref> and the president of the Israel Chemical Society (2006-2009).<ref>[http://www.chemistry.org.il/ Israel Chemical Society (ICS)]</ref> The [[Israel Academy of Sciences and Humanities]] designated him to be the Israeli chairman of the National Committee of Chemistry towards [[International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry|IUPAC]] during 2010-2013. In addition, during 2014-2017 he served as the president and head of the [[Givat Washington|Washington]] [[List of Israeli universities and colleges#Colleges|College for Education]], Yavne.<ref>[http://www.washington.ac.il/michlala/ Givat Washington College of Education]</ref> In 2016, Prof. Margel was chosen to lead the establishment of a new agro-nanotechnology center in the [[Agricultural Research Organization, Volcani Center|Volcani Institute for Agriculture]], Beit Dagan.<ref>[http://www.agri.gov.il/en/home/default.aspx Agricultural Research Organization, Volcani Center]</ref><ref>[http://www.agri.gov.il/download/volcanipedia/Content/Eng/Vv4/#PDF/1 ''Volcani Voice'', Vol.4, September 2017]</ref>

==Scientific interests and publications==
Margel earlier interests included [[electrochemistry]] of [[Vinyl polymer|vinylic]] [[monomer]] and polymers,<ref name="FlanaganMargel1978">{{cite journal|last1=Flanagan|first1=James B.|last2=Margel|first2=Shlomo|last3=Bard|first3=Allen J.|last4=Anson|first4=Fred C.|title=Electron transfer to and from molecules containing multiple, noninteracting redox centers. Electrochemical oxidation of poly(vinylferrocene)|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=100|issue=13|year=1978|pages=4248–4253|issn=0002-7863|doi=10.1021/ja00481a040}}</ref> polyaldehyde [[Microparticle#Microspheres|microspheres]]<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Margel |first1=S. |last2=Beitler |first2=U. |last3=Offarim |first3=M. |date=1982 |title=Polyacrolein microspheres as a new tool in cell biology |url=http://jcs.biologists.org/content/56/1/157 |journal=Journal of Cell Science |volume=56 |issue=1 |pages=157–175 |doi=10.1242/jcs.56.1.157 |pmid=7166562 |url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Margel |first1=S. |last2=Marcus |first2=L. |date=1989 |title=Specific Hemoperfusion Therapy |journal=Chemtech |volume=19 |pages=238 }}</ref> and self-assembly monolayers.<ref name="MargelVogler1993">{{cite journal|last1=Margel|first1=S.|last2=Vogler|first2=E. A.|last3=Firment|first3=L.|last4=Watt|first4=T.|last5=Haynie|first5=S.|last6=Sogah|first6=D. Y.|title=Peptide, protein, and cellular interactions with self-assembled monolayer model surfaces|journal=Journal of Biomedical Materials Research|volume=27|issue=12|year=1993|pages=1463–1476|issn=0021-9304|doi=10.1002/jbm.820271202|pmid=8113233}}</ref>
His current research focuses on [[Functional polymers|functional polymeric]] nano/[[Microparticle|micro-particles]] for [[Nanomedicine|medical]]<ref name="SkaatChen2012">{{cite journal|last1=Skaat|first1=Hadas|last2=Chen|first2=Ravit|last3=Grinberg|first3=Igor|last4=Margel|first4=Shlomo|title=Engineered Polymer Nanoparticles Containing Hydrophobic Dipeptide for Inhibition of Amyloid-β Fibrillation|journal=Biomacromolecules|volume=13|issue=9|year=2012|pages=2662–2670|issn=1525-7797|doi=10.1021/bm3011177|pmid=22897679}}</ref><ref name="Rudnick-GlickCorem-Salkmon2015">{{cite journal|last1=Rudnick-Glick|first1=S.|last2=Corem-Salkmon|first2=E.|last3=Grinberg|first3=I.|last4=Yehuda|first4=R.|last5=Margel|first5=S.|title=Near IR fluorescent conjugated poly(ethylene glycol)bisphosphonate nanoparticles for in vivo bone targeting in a young mouse model|journal=Journal of Nanobiotechnology|volume=13|issue=1|year=2015|page=80|issn=1477-3155|doi=10.1186/s12951-015-0126-0|pmid=26577112|pmc=4650844 |doi-access=free }}</ref> and [[Industrial applications of nanotechnology|industrial applications]],<ref name="TalRudnick-Glick2018">{{cite journal|last1=Tal|first1=Nimrod|last2=Rudnick-Glick|first2=Safra|last3=Grinberg|first3=Igor|last4=Natan|first4=Michal|last5=Banin|first5=Ehud|last6=Margel|first6=Shlomo|title=Engineering of a New Bisphosphonate Monomer and Nanoparticles of Narrow Size Distribution for Antibacterial Applications|journal=ACS Omega|volume=3|issue=2|year=2018|pages=1458–1469|issn=2470-1343|doi=10.1021/acsomega.7b01686|doi-access=free|pmid=30023805|pmc=6044825}}</ref> [[surface modification]],<ref name="MargelCohen1992">{{cite journal|last1=Margel|first1=Shlomo|last2=Cohen|first2=Ella|last3=Dolitzky|first3=Yehudit|last4=Sivan|first4=Orit|title=Surface modification. I. Polyacrolein microspheres covalently bonded onto polyethylene|journal=Journal of Polymer Science Part A: Polymer Chemistry|volume=30|issue=6|year=1992|pages=1103–1110|issn=0887-624X|doi=10.1002/pola.1992.080300617}}</ref><ref name="BrandrissMargel1993">{{cite journal|last1=Brandriss|first1=Sergio|last2=Margel|first2=Shlomo|title=Synthesis and characterization of self-assembled hydrophobic monolayer coatings on silica colloids|journal=Langmuir|volume=9|issue=5|year=1993|pages=1232–1240|issn=0743-7463|doi=10.1021/la00029a014}}</ref> and [[Thin film|functional thin]] [[coating]]s (self-cleaning,<ref name="GutmanNatan2014">{{cite journal|last1=Gutman|first1=Ori|last2=Natan|first2=Michal|last3=Banin|first3=Ehud|last4=Margel|first4=Shlomo|title=Characterization and antibacterial properties of N-halamine-derivatized cross-linked polymethacrylamide nanoparticles|journal=Biomaterials|volume=35|issue=19|year=2014|pages=5079–5087|issn=0142-9612|doi=10.1016/j.biomaterials.2014.02.056|pmid=24695094}}</ref> [[Biofouling|anti-biofouling]],<ref name="NatanGutman2015">{{cite journal|last1=Natan|first1=Michal|last2=Gutman|first2=Ori|last3=Lavi|first3=Ronit|last4=Margel|first4=Shlomo|last5=Banin|first5=Ehud|title=Killing Mechanism of Stable N-Halamine Cross-Linked Polymethacrylamide Nanoparticles That Selectively Target Bacteria|journal=ACS Nano|volume=9|issue=2|year=2015|pages=1175–1188|issn=1936-0851|doi=10.1021/nn507168x|pmid=25602279}}</ref> [[Polymer stabilizers#UV absorbers|UV absorbers]],<ref name="CohenHaham2016">{{cite journal|last1=Cohen|first1=Sarit|last2=Haham|first2=Hai|last3=Pellach|first3=Michal|last4=Margel|first4=Shlomo|title=Design of UV-Absorbing Polypropylene Films with Polymeric Benzotriaziole Based Nano- and Microparticle Coatings|journal=ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces|volume=9|issue=1|year=2016|pages=868–875|issn=1944-8244|doi=10.1021/acsami.6b12821|pmid=28005334}}</ref> [[anti-fog]]ging<ref>S. Margel, M, Kolitz Domb, et.al. "Proteinoid compounds, process of preparing same and uses thereof". US patent application 0042827 (2017).</ref> and [[superhydrophobic coating]]s<ref>S. Margel, Sharon Bretler, Sarit Cohen and Naftali Kanovsky. "In-situ thin coating of silica particles onto plastic films and their applications" US Provisional Patent Application No. 62/645,839 (2018).</ref>).
Prof. Margel is a world pioneer and gained international reputation in the area of [[nanotechnology]], particularly in the design of [[nanotechnology#Functional approaches|functional]] nano- and micrometer-sized [[Nanoparticle|particles]] of very narrow size distribution for [[Nanomedicine|medical]] and [[Industrial applications of nanotechnology|industrial applications]]. Many of his publications were collected to a book titled "Recent advances in polymers & nanotechnology".<ref>{{cite book |last1=Margel |first1=Shlomo |title=Recent advances in polymers & nanotechnology |date=2022 |publisher=Index of sciences |location=London |isbn=9798836372194}}</ref>

During his career, Prof. Margel supervised over 100 students. He has over 300 peer-reviewed articles in print, which were cited nearly 8,100 times. Margel has published many book chapters on various aspects of nanoparticles and functional thin coatings, won about 75 national and international research grants and has about 40 [[patent]]s and patent applications.<ref>[https://scholar.google.co.il/citations?user=YkruYiYAAAAJ&hl=en Shlomo Margel, Google Scholar]</ref><ref name=exact>[https://www.biu.ac.il/ESC/shlomo_margel.htm Prof. Shlomo Margel's website, Bar-Ilan Faculty of Exact Sciences]</ref>

Among his previous awards were the [[Chaim Weizmann|Dr. Chaim Weizmann]] Postdoctoral Fellowship for Scientific Research, established by the Myron A. Bantrell Trust (1976-1978); Shmuel Yaroslavsky Memorial Prize for Study on the Development of [[Microparticle#Microspheres|Microspheres]] for [[Nanomedicine|Medical Applications]], awarded by the Scientific Committee of the Weizmann Institute of Science (1984); M. Landau Grant Foundation for Achievement in the Area of Polymers, awarded by [[Mifal HaPayis]] (1989); Taubenblat Prize for studies on [[Dressing (medical)#Bioactive products|Bioactive Wound Dressing]] & Particles (2003); The Elias, Genevieve and Georgianna Atol Charitable Trust Fellow in [[Nanomedicine]] (2003)  and the Israel Vacuum Society (IVS)<ref>[http://www.ivs.org.il/ The Israel Vacuum Society (IVS)]</ref> Excellency Award for Research (2014).<ref name=exact />

==Personal life==
Shlomo Margel is married to Hannah Margel, a Ph.D. in [[Science education|Science Teaching]] from the Weizmann Institute of Science.<ref name="MargelEylon2008">{{cite journal|last1=Margel|first1=Hannah|last2=Eylon|first2=Bat-Sheva|last3=Scherz|first3=Zahava|title=A longitudinal study of junior high school students' conceptions of the structure of materials|journal=[[Journal of Research in Science Teaching]]|volume=45|issue=1|year=2008|pages=132–152|issn=0022-4308|doi=10.1002/tea.20214}}</ref> They live in [[Rehovot]] and have four children and seven grandchildren. His sister is former MK [[Gila Finkelstein]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=חרותי-סובר |first1=טלי |title=גילה פינקלשטיין, ועדת טירקל והאח הנשיא |url=https://www.haaretz.co.il/blogs/taliherutisover/2015-10-07/ty-article/0000017f-f8ab-d460-afff-fbefefa90000 |access-date=27 July 2026 |work=[[Haaretz]] |date=7 October 2015}}</ref>
